research_domain: Dark-web claims of organizational data exposure

research_questions: What types of organizational data exposure are advertised or discussed?
Which sectors and broad geographic regions are mentioned?
What evidence do sources claim to offer, without collecting exposed records?
Which claims recur across sources and which materially change over time?
scope.claim_handling: Treat source statements as unverified claims; do not infer breach authenticity or dark-web prevalence.
include: Primary-source items asserting an existing exposure involving a specific organization or identifiable organizational dataset.
Specific listings asserting possession or sale of an existing organizational dataset, without obtaining its contents.
First-party exposure announcements with supporting text establishing the affected organization or dataset relationship.
exclude: Generic advertising, unrelated discussion, and claims too vague to classify.
Repeated observations without meaningful content changes; preserve query matches and collection history.
Exposed datasets, sample records, credentials, downloadable archives, and attachments.
Sources requiring account creation, payment, or interaction with source operators.
Secondary news reporting and articles about third-party incidents; retain only as separate background if needed.
Educational guides and tutorials about hacking, credentials, forensics, or breaches.
Generic service/capability advertisements, hypothetical target companies, and provider or publisher names without an affected-organization relationship.
scope.source_access: Text-based results and accessible pages discoverable through Robin.

collection_dates.date_setup: Set explicit start and end dates before collection; the seven-day window is a scheduling allowance, not recurring collection.
collection_dates.undated_findings: Retain relevant undated findings with publication date unknown.
collection_dates.timestamp_policy: Record UTC collection timestamps separately from source-claimed publication dates.

page_collection.fetch_when: Title and snippet cannot establish relevance or support the research fields.
page_collection.truncation_policy: Mark truncated content explicitly; do not infer that missing text was absent from the source.

observation.row_definition: One distinct source item and its materially distinct content.
observation.multiple_query_matches: Keep one observation with associations to every matching query.
observation.meaningful_change: Create a new observation for a changed claim, exposure description, or substantive status update at the same URL.
observation.nonmeaningful_change: Formatting changes and repeated retrievals update history without creating a finding.
observation.cross_source_claims: Keep separate source observations; optionally associate them with an incident-group identifier.
observation.near_duplicates: Flag for review rather than automatically merging.

limitations: Documents discoverable claims and their evolution; does not verify breaches or exposed-data authenticity.
English-only queries and unavailable sources limit coverage.
Search results are not a representative sample of the entire dark web.

limits.limit_policy: Enforce every applicable limit; stop extracted text at whichever byte or character cap is reached first.

sanitization.implementation_status: Live capture retains finite labels and keyed role/evidence pseudonyms; supporting quotes remain in expiring private memory. Regex redaction alone does not establish privacy or relevance.
sanitization.key_storage: Store separately from source control, datasets, and logs; reuse the key for authorized longitudinal matching.
sanitization.raw_urls: Default to no persistence. If retracing is necessary, use restricted provenance storage with the same retention limit as raw content.
sanitization.export_source_details: Export a source pseudonym; include a sanitized URL only if necessary and reviewed for residual identifiers.
sanitization.unsanitized_storage: Restricted temporary storage only; delete no later than seven days after collection.
sanitization.review: Review relevance, near duplicates, and residual sensitive information before distributing the dataset.

dataset.schema_status: The reviewed live CSV schema is implemented in release.py and its generated data dictionary; proposed free-text fields remain withheld.

query_management.refinement_policy: Record original and Robin-refined queries; review refinements for preserved meaning during the pilot.
query_management.freeze_policy: Freeze reviewed queries and settings for the pilot; version subsequent changes.
query_management.review_example: An announcement claiming an organizational database exposure can qualify; a generic marketplace advertisement without a specific exposure claim does not.
query_management.expected_effect: Retrieve claim-level metadata and summaries while excluding exposed records and downloads.
query_management.enablement: Scope tightened by the project owner after reviewing the three readable pilot pages. Queries remain disabled pending successful primary-source relevance validation.
